battle.name: 長安之戰
battle.brief: 廣明元年（880）十一月黃巢陷東都洛陽，十二月西進，六日激戰而下潼關、華州，僖宗倉皇奔蜀，叛軍入長安建大齊，歲內改元金統。卡上亞述長弓不在此戰，弓兵開路、車兵跟進的體制足為對照：真正決定長安陷落的是諸道兵調度、禁軍崩解與糧道，不是弓弩本身。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 廣明元年（880）冬，長安之戰實際上是唐王朝中央軍系與黃巢「齊」軍在關中的一次總崩潰。作戰一方是唐廷及它所依賴的諸道節度使聯軍：禁軍之中的神策軍由宦官田令孜直接掌握，京師宿衞主力在出征與分割中被抽調一空；忠武、昭義、河中、興元等軍各領本部兵自保，互相不能節制；劍南、河東諸道奉詔勤王，卻各懷異志。另一方是起於曹州私鹽群體的黃巢軍，舊史稱「齊」，以尚讓主持幕府，四品以下唐官留任，中樞設太尉兼中書令、侍中與尚書左右僕射。叛軍並非一個國家，而是由河南淮北流民、鹽丁、散兵以及望風歸附的州縣兵拼湊而成，號稱百萬而精銳有限。戰場在關中：東都洛陽至西都長安一線，含潼關、華州、灞上三處要點，以及長安城與宮城本身。兩個陣營的本質差別，是唐廷有城池與糧倉而無統一指揮，叛軍有統一指揮而無固定根據地。
countriesEn: In the winter of 880 the battle for Chang'an was in fact a general collapse of the Tang central command system against Huang Chao's army of the state of Qi in the Guanzhong corridor. On one side stood the imperial court at Chang'an together with the circuit-governor armies it depended on: the Shence Guard within the palace troops was under the personal control of the eunuch Tian Lingzi, and the greater part of the metropolitan garrison had been thinned out by detachments sent abroad or handed over to other commands; the armies of Zhongwu, Zhaoyi, Hezhong and Xingyuan each held their own men, obeyed no common commander, and were unwilling to cross swords with each other; the contingents of Jiannan, Hedong and other circuits answered the call for aid but pursued their own private interests. On the other side stood Huang Chao's host, styled Qi in the old histories, with a civil administration headed by Shang Rang; Tang officials of the fourth rank and below were kept in their posts, and the central offices were filled by a chancellor-in-chief, a palace director and two vice chancellors. The rebel force was not a state but a coalition pieced together from salt smugglers' bands in Henan, famine migrants, deserters and the troops of surrendered prefectures: it claimed a hundred thousand men, yet its seasoned core was small. The theatre of operations ran from the eastern capital of Luoyang to the western capital of Chang'an, with Tong Pass, Huazhou and Bashang as the three hinge points, and with the city and palace of Chang'an as the prize. The essential difference between the two coalitions is simple: the Tang had walls and granaries but no unified command; the rebels had a unified command but no fixed base.
people: 黃巢（835至884），曹州冤句人，私鹽商家庭出身，乾符二年（875）起兵時自稱衝天大將軍，克長安後於含元殿即位，國號大齊、改元金統，其後兵敗退保泰山狼虎谷，餘眾潰散，他本人亦死於亂軍之中。叛軍幕府由尚讓主持，尚讓後任大齊太尉兼中書令；趙璋任侍中，孟楷、蓋洪分任尚書左、右僕射，皮日休為翰林學士，替黃巢起草文告。唐廷一方，僖宗李儇在叛軍逼近時由宦官田令孜挾持出奔劍南，行在設於成都；宰相盧攜在僖宗西走後仰藥自盡；淮南節度使高駢擁兵十餘萬而坐觀成敗，屢為時論所譏。僖宗西遷途中由諸道武臣接續入覲，882年朱溫以同州降唐，883年沙陀將領李克用率兵南下，與河中、忠武兵力合擊，扭轉了戰局；此後主持收復京畿者，正是李克用與其沙陀騎兵。
peopleEn: Huang Chao (835 to 884) was a native of Yuanju in Caozhou, born into a family of salt smugglers. When he raised his banner in 875, during the second year of the Qianfu era, he styled himself the General Who Charges to Heaven; after taking Chang'an he was enthroned in the Hall of Contained Origin, founded the state of Qi and changed the era name to Jintong. Later, defeated, he withdrew to the Langhu Valley by Mount Tai, his remaining host dissolved, and he himself perished amid his own disorderly troops. The rebel administration was headed by Shang Rang, who afterwards held the posts of chancellor-in-chief and director of the central secretariat of Qi; Zhao Zhang was made palace director, Meng Kai and Gai Hong took the two vice chancellorship, and Pi Rixiu served as Hanlin academician, drafting Huang Chao's proclamations. On the Tang side, Emperor Xizong Li Xuan was carried off toward Jiannan by the eunuch Tian Lingzi as the rebel host drew near, and the travelling court was established at Chengdu; the chancellor Lu Kuo, once the emperor had fled west, swallowed poison and died; the Huaainan circuit governor Gao Pian held more than a hundred thousand troops and sat still watching the outcome, an obvious target of contemporary criticism. As the emperor's flight continued, the military governors of the circuits presented themselves to him one after another; in 882 Zhu Wen came over to the Tang with his command at Tongzhou, and in 883 the Shatuo commander Li Keyong marched south and, joined with the armies of Hezhong and Zhongwu, reversed the course of the war. It was Li Keyong and his Shatuo cavalry who afterwards directed the recovery of the capital region.
kits: 卡上這件亞述長弓（約公元前700年）並不出現在唐末的長安，它是亞述「弓兵開路、車兵跟進」體制的代表，用來對照本戰的投射火力。亞述的長弓是當時已知射程最遠的弓之一，單兵拉力大，弓兵常在車上射擊，先以箭幕壓住對方陣線與城門，車兵再進抵殘殺；它體現的是「以投射火力換取前進空間」這個通則。中原唐軍與叛軍並不靠這樣的長弓取勝。唐廷可用的是弩：擲婦機一類的連射器械、軸弩與小型弩機架在城頭與陣前，射程雖短而精準，與弓兵構成層次；近身是環首刀、長槊、陌刀，配皮甲與少量鐵甲；守城用障城、拒馬、鹿角與飛石機（配將砲一類的拋射器）。叛軍則走輕裝：步卒執刀矛、標槍與投石，配騎兵巡掠，靠流動與襲擾取勝，攻城則用撞車、飛石與穴地，極少正面填壕。兩軍都靠鼓噪與旗號配合行動，糧食方面，唐廷靠汴河漕運、洛陽倉儲與蜀地輸糧，牛、驢與船隻是主要運力；叛軍沒有漕運，只能沿途州縣就地徵發，這與亞述那種有底格里斯河漕運支撐、可以長期駐紮的體系恰成對比。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow shown on the card, dated to about 700 BC, never appeared at Chang'an in the late Tang; it stands for the Assyrian system in which the bowmen open the way and the chariotry follows, and is used here to set against the projecting firepower of this battle. The Assyrian long bow was among the longest-ranged bows then known, it demanded great draw weight from a single man, and its archers commonly shot from the chariot platform, laying down an arrow screen against the enemy line and the gates before the chariots closed in; it embodies the general rule of buying forward space with missile fire. Neither the Tang army nor the rebels won with a bow of that kind. What the Tang had was the crossbow: light repeating engines of the zhifu-ji type, windlass crossbows and small swivel bows set on the walls and in front of the line, short in range but accurate, layered together with the ordinary bowmen; at close quarters were ring-pommel sabres, long spears and the miao dao, with leather armour and a little iron; for defence they used obstructions, caltrops, deer-horn barricades and stone-throwing engines of the peijiang-pao type. The rebels marched light instead: infantry with knives, spears, javelins and thrown stones, accompanied by cavalry out on long sweeps, winning by movement and harassment, and at the walls they used battering beams, stone-throwers and mining, seldom filling ditches in a frontal rush. Both sides moved to drum-beats and banners, and on supply the Tang drew on the Bian canal, the granaries of Luoyang and grain shipped in from Shu, with oxen, donkeys and boats as the main carriers; the rebels had no canal system and had to take what the prefectures along the route could give, which is the exact opposite of the Assyrian model sustained by Tigris river transport and permanent bases.
tactics: 這一戰的戰術，關鍵不在單點交鋒，而在時間差與空間縱深。黃巢軍放棄南方經營已久的州縣，捨棄嶺南的糧源與根據地，率大隊輕裝北進，專挑唐廷防線最薄的一段：汝州、洛陽一線既無重兵集結，淮南高駢又按兵不動，朝廷更在關鍵時分遣諸道兵。攻下洛陽之後，叛軍不設防、不停留，十餘日內西進，六日激戰而下潼關；關城守軍與監軍先行潰散，華州一日而陷，兵鋒直抵灞上。黃巢入城後軍紀一度整肅：不掠財貨，也不急於追擊西奔的僖宗，反而讓唐廷得到喘息重整的時間，其後兵事才急轉直下。唐廷方面的戰術則散亂：京師宿衞被分割出征，各道節度使各自為戰，無統一指揮，潼關至長安的防線其實只剩空殼。撤退規劃上，僖宗放棄西都以東與關中全部城邑，走金牛道經興元入劍南，行程二千餘里，等於把國都交給叛軍。叛軍的攻城手段集中在撞車、飛石與穴地，而防守方的飛石機與障城，多因守將先走而未能發揮。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this battle turn less on any single clash than on differences in timing and in depth of space. Huang Chao's army abandoned the prefectures it had worked for years in the south and left behind the food and the bases of Lingnan, then marched north in a large but lightly equipped column, choosing precisely the one stretch where the Tang defence was thinnest: the line of Ruzhou and Luoyang had no heavy troops concentrated, Huaainan governor Gao Pian sat still, and the court had at the crucial moment disbanded the armies of the circuits. After taking Luoyang the rebels did not dig in and did not pause; within a little more than ten days they drove west, and after six days of hard fighting Tong Pass fell. The garrison and the imperial commissioner there broke before the assault, Huazhou was lost in a single day, and the column reached Bashang. On entering the city Huang Chao's troops were for a time disciplined: they did not plunder, and they did not pursue the fleeing Xizong, which gave the Tang court the breathing space to reorganise before events turned decisively against it. The Tang side, by contrast, fought no coherent plan: the metropolitan garrison had been split off to the front, the circuit governors fought their own separate war without a common commander, and the defensive line between Tong Pass and Chang'an was in truth an empty shell. As for the flight, Xizong gave up every city east of the western capital and the whole of Guanzhong, took the Jinniu Road through Xingyuan into Jiannan, and travelled more than two thousand li, in effect handing the capital over to the rebels. The rebel siege methods centred on battering beams, stone-throwers and mining, while the defenders' stone-throwing engines and barricades mostly failed to get into action because their commanders had already run.
data: 可核對的數字有限，只列史籍明確記載者。起兵規模：乾符二年（875）黃巢在曹州起兵時，兵眾以數千計；乾符五年（878）五月王仙芝死後，其部眾與歸附州縣兵相合，人數才以萬計。進攻節奏：乾符六年（879）九月克廣州，廣明元年（880）八月渡淮，十月克申州，十一月十七日克東都洛陽；自洛陽西進「僅激戰六日」，十二月初三下潼關、初四下華州，旋即抵灞上；十二月中旬入長安，十二月十一日於含元殿即位，號大齊、改元金統。距離：洛陽至長安的道路近千里，潼關至長安不足三百里，所以關門一失，京畿在數日之內便無可守之地。西行：僖宗自長安至成都逾二千餘里，耗時逾月，途中仍以行在名義發號施令。佔領期：黃巢軍控制長安自881年初至883年四月撤出，前後約兩年四個月；其後李克用率沙陀兵一萬餘人南下，華州、藍田相繼失守，陳州被圍近三百日，黃巢敗走商山、泰山，餘眾潰散。
dataEn: The verifiable numbers are limited, and only those plainly recorded in the histories are given here. Scale of the rising: when Huang Chao raised his banner at Caozhou in 875, the second year of the Qianfu era, his following numbered only several thousand; it was after the death of Wang Xianzhi in the fifth month of 878 that his own men and the troops of surrendered prefectures combined and the force could be counted in tens of thousands. Rhythm of the advance: Guangzhou was taken in the ninth month of 879; the Huai River was crossed in the eighth month of 880; Shenzhou fell in the tenth month; the eastern capital of Luoyang was taken on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month. From Luoyang the drive west took only six days of hard fighting: Tong Pass on the third day of the twelfth month, Huazhou on the fourth, and the column was soon at Bashang. The city of Chang'an was entered in the middle of the twelfth month, and on the eleventh day of that month the occupier was enthroned in the Hall of Contained Origin, founding the state of Qi and changing the era to Jintong. Distances: the road from Luoyang to Chang'an is close to a thousand li, and from Tong Pass to Chang'an less than three hundred, so once the pass was lost the capital region had nothing left to hold within a few days. The flight west: Xizong covered more than two thousand li from Chang'an to Chengdu, taking over a month, and continued to issue orders in the name of the travelling court. Period of occupation: Huang Chao's army held Chang'an from early 881 until its withdrawal in the fourth month of 883, roughly two years and four months; after that Li Keyong marched south with more than ten thousand Shatuo men, Huazhou and Lantian fell in turn, the siege of Chenzhou lasted close to three hundred days, and Huang Chao was driven back through the Shang Mountains towards Mount Tai, where his host came apart.
cause: 長安之戰的起因，是唐廷多年積累的財政、軍制與人事矛盾同時爆發。咸通以來，兩稅之外又加各種雜斂，州縣為完成上供而橫徵；河南水旱連年，饑民大批流亡。乾符元年（874）王仙芝起兵於長垣，乾符二年黃巢以私鹽眾起於曹州冤句。朝廷先遣宋威、曾元裕討之，屢勝而縱之；又屢次招安，黃巢怒責王仙芝「獨取官而去，使這五千餘眾何所歸乎」，集團遂無退路。關鍵在兩次誤判：一是朝廷倚賴淮南節度使高駢，卻任其擁兵觀望，坐失洛陽；二是宰相盧攜在黃巢詐降期間竟遣散諸道兵，使唐廷在關中只剩禁軍一人可用。而禁軍主力早已在前線耗損，或被田令孜分割給外鎮，京師遂無守備之兵。加之唐廷與藩鎮互不信任、節度使各自割據，一旦長安有警，數日之間即無援兵可到。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the battle for Chang'an lay in fiscal, military and personnel contradictions that had accumulated inside the Tang for years and then broke at once. Since the Xiantong reign, miscellaneous levies had been piled on top of the two-tax system, and the prefectures squeezed the countryside to meet the fixed remittances; in Henan, drought and flood followed one another for years and famine migrants moved about in large numbers. In 874, the first year of Qianfu, Wang Xianzhi raised troops at Changyuan; in the following year Huang Chao rose at Yuanju in Caozhou with a band of salt smugglers. The court first sent Song Wei and Zeng Yuanyu against them and repeatedly let them go after winning, and it made offer after offer of pardon, until Huang Chao reproached Wang Xianzhi for taking office alone and leaving five thousand men without a future, and the band had no way back. Two misjudgements mattered most. First, the court relied on Huaainan governor Gao Pian and let him sit on his army and watch, thereby losing Luoyang. Second, while Huang Chao was feigning surrender the chancellor Lu Kuo actually disbanded the armies of the circuits, so that in Guanzhong the Tang had nothing left but the palace troops. And the greater part of those palace troops had already been spent on the frontier or handed out to regional commands by the eunuch Tian Lingzi, so the capital was left without a single defender. Add to this the fact that court and circuit governors did not trust one another, each governor ruling his own ground, and when Chang'an sounded the alarm there was no relief army within reach for days on end.
impact: 長安之戰的直接後果，是唐王朝失去關中根基與政治中心。僖宗西幸成都，朝廷自此以行在發號施令，藩鎮的割據由暗中坐大變為公開各行其是：河中王重榮、忠武張全義、昭義孟方立、河東李克用、宣武朱溫先後以勤王為名各掌一方兵柄，擁兵自重，朝廷對節度使的約束力自此基本瓦解。另一條線索是朱溫：他在882年以同州降唐，隨即受賜名全忠，成為唐廷對付黃巢與收復兩京的主要出力者，也因此在亂平之後坐大，終於907年篡唐建後梁，開五代之局。沙陀人李克用據河東，與朱溫相抗，成為五代北面的主要勢力。至於城本身，長安在戰中反覆易手，宮禁府庫為空，官方政治中心後來東移至洛陽、開封，唐長安城從此再未恢復舊觀。黃巢之亂造成的整體國力耗損，使唐廷再也無力解決節度使問題，成為唐朝崩解的加速劑。
impactEn: The direct consequence of the battle was the loss by the Tang of its Guanzhong base and its political centre. Xizong fled west to Chengdu, and from then on the court governed in the name of the travelling court, while the secession of the military governors turned from something that grew by stealth into something practised openly: Wang Chongrong of Hezhong, Zhang Quanyi of Zhongwu, Meng Fangli of Zhaoyi, Li Keyong of Hedong and Zhu Wen of Xuanwu each took the military authority of his own region in the name of aiding the emperor, kept their troops, and the court's hold over the circuit governors was henceforth broken in all but name. A second thread is that of Zhu Wen: by surrendering at Tongzhou in 882 he was received into the Tang service and given the name Quanzhong, and he became the chief instrument by which the court fought Huang Chao and recovered the two capitals, and therefore grew strong after the rebellion was settled, until in 907 he took the throne and founded Later Liang, opening the Five Dynasties. The Shatuo Li Keyong, entrenched in Hedong, matched Zhu Wen from the north and became the principal northern power of that age. As for the city itself, Chang'an changed hands repeatedly during the war and the palace stores were emptied; the official political centre later moved east to Luoyang and to Kaifeng, and Tang Chang'an never recovered its former aspect. The overall drain of state strength inflicted by the Huang Chao rebellion left the Tang unable to solve the problem of the military governors at all, and became the accelerant of the dynasty's collapse.
result: 結果是叛軍的全面勝利與唐廷的全面撤退。黃巢軍入長安後，以大齊名號建元金統，留用四品以下朝官，尚讓、趙璋、孟楷、蓋洪分掌中樞，尚讓以布告曉諭市人安分，初期軍紀尚整；但占據兩京之後，軍隊旋即在城內縱兵抄掠，宮禁府庫為空，留長安的宗室與朝官多被清除，史稱「洗城」。882年唐軍一度反攻長安，叛軍先退灞上，唐軍入城後大肆縱掠，黃巢當夜回師反攻，把官軍驅出城外，此後關中反覆拉鋸，雙方都未能長久據守。882年九月，朱溫在同州與河中王重榮交鋒中降唐；883年沙陀李克用率兵一萬餘人南下，華州、藍田相繼陷落，四月黃巢撤出長安入商山，往陳州、蔡州方向流竄，陳州之圍歷時近三百日，最終退至泰山狼虎谷，餘眾潰散，黃巢亦死於亂軍。此役之後，關中再無可用之兵與糧，唐廷雖於883年復得長安，卻已是一個只剩行在與藩鎮的殘缺朝廷。
resultEn: The result was a complete rebel victory and a complete Tang withdrawal. After the army entered Chang'an, the new state of Qi was proclaimed with the era name Jintong, officials of the fourth rank and below were retained, and the central offices were divided between Shang Rang, Zhao Zhang, Meng Kai and Gai Hong; Shang Rang issued notices telling the townspeople to stay at their work, and the army's discipline was at first orderly. Once the two capitals were held, however, the troops were soon plundering inside the walls, the palace stores were emptied, and the Tang clansmen and officers who remained in the city were largely killed off, an episode recorded as the washing of the city. In 882 the Tang forces counter-attacked Chang'an; the rebels first withdrew to Bashang, but the Tang soldiers who entered the capital gave themselves over to indiscriminate plunder, and Huang Chao turned back that very night, drove the government troops out again, and from then on the two sides fought back and forth in Guanzhong, neither able to hold the city for long. In the ninth month of 882 Zhu Wen came over to the Tang at Tongzhou while fighting Wang Chongrong of Hezhong; in 883 the Shatuo chieftain Li Keyong marched south with more than ten thousand men, Huazhou and Lantian fell in turn, and in the fourth month Huang Chao withdrew from Chang'an into the Shang Mountains and drifted towards Chenzhou and Caizhou. The siege of Chenzhou lasted close to three hundred days; in the end he was driven back to the Langhu Valley by Mount Tai, his host came apart, and Huang Chao died amid his own disorderly men. After this the Guanzhong region had neither soldiers nor grain left to speak of, and although the Tang court recovered Chang'an in 883, it was already a truncated government with nothing but the travelling court and the regional governors.
